boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Northwestern rituals, performances, celebrations and game-day practices rooted in Evanston campus life.

cards.title: Paint the Rock
cards.subtitle: The Rock, South Campus
cards.notes: See the Rock in daylight, then check the University’s guidance before planning a painting or a 24-hour guard shift with your group.
cards.short_summary: A former Class of 1902 fountain became Northwestern’s public canvas for student expression.
cards.evidence_claim: Northwestern says painting the Rock began as a student prank in the 1940s; students now use it for slogans, student groups, activism and celebrations, with guarding used to earn painting rights.
cards.access_notes: The University describes the Rock as student-moderated; follow current campus policies and any reservation requirements.

cards.title: March Through the Arch
cards.subtitle: Arnold Weber Arch, Wildcat Welcome
cards.notes: If you are an incoming student, join your Peer Adviser group for the official procession; visitors can watch along the designated route.
cards.short_summary: New and transfer students cross Weber Arch together to mark their entry into Northwestern.
cards.evidence_claim: Northwestern describes March Through the Arch as a fall procession led by the marching band in which incoming students symbolically begin their college experience.
cards.source_title: March Through the Arch: Northwestern University
cards.access_notes: This is a Wildcat Welcome activity for incoming students; consult the current orientation schedule for participation details.

cards.title: March Back Through the Arch
cards.subtitle: Arnold Weber Arch, graduation season
cards.notes: Graduating students should use the official graduation-weekend schedule and gather only through announced class or school arrangements.
cards.short_summary: Seniors retrace the welcome procession in reverse before graduation.
cards.evidence_claim: Northwestern states that graduating seniors repeat the Arch procession before graduation by retracing the incoming route, a practice called Marching Back Through the Arch.
cards.source_title: March Through the Arch: Northwestern University
cards.access_notes: Participation occurs before graduation; use the current graduation-weekend schedule for timing and assembly instructions.

cards.title: Dillo Day
cards.subtitle: Northwestern lakefront, spring
cards.notes: Follow Mayfest’s official announcements for the current lineup, entry rules and schedule; enjoy the music festival through its posted event procedures.
cards.short_summary: The campus’s spring music celebration evolved from an event called Armadillo Day.
cards.evidence_claim: Northwestern identifies Dillo Day as an annual student-run music festival on the University lakefront that began as Armadillo Day.
cards.access_notes: Festival logistics and eligibility can change by year; consult the official event organizer for current rules.

cards.title: Dance Marathon
cards.subtitle: Annual campus philanthropy event
cards.notes: Look for the current Dance Marathon volunteer, fundraising and attendance information, then choose a role that fits your schedule and access needs.
cards.short_summary: Students gather to dance and fundraise for charitable beneficiaries.
cards.evidence_claim: Northwestern’s history page says Dance Marathon has run since 1975 and that students gather each spring for 15 hours of dancing for a cause.
cards.access_notes: Beneficiaries, venue and participation procedures change; verify the current Dance Marathon information before attending or registering.

cards.title: The Waa-Mu Show
cards.subtitle: Northwestern’s annual original musical
cards.notes: Check the Wirtz Center’s current production page for show dates and ticket details, or explore the tradition through its documented student-made format.
cards.short_summary: An annual original musical is written, performed and presented by Northwestern students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Wirtz Center calls the Waa-Mu Show Northwestern’s oldest theatrical tradition and says students create an original musical each year; the name reflects the 1929 W.A.A. and M.U. collaboration.
cards.access_notes: Performance dates, venue and ticket requirements vary by production; confirm the current listing before going.

cards.title: Run the Wildcat Dash
cards.subtitle: First home football game tradition
cards.notes: Eligible first-years should follow the current game-day instructions for the official run across the field into the student section.
cards.short_summary: Incoming first-years make their first Ryan Field entrance by crossing the playing surface together.
cards.evidence_claim: Northwestern Athletics describes the Wildcat Dash as a tradition in which incoming first-years run across the field to the student section when entering Ryan Field for the first time.
cards.source_title: Gameday Central: 'Cats Welcome Back Students With Night Game vs. Minnesota
cards.access_notes: This is for incoming first-years at the designated football game; current stadium and game-day procedures apply.

cards.title: Make the Wildcat Growl
cards.subtitle: Northwestern game-day cheer
cards.notes: Learn the cheer from the official athletics song page, then join it when prompted at a Northwestern sporting event.
cards.short_summary: The Wildcat Growl is one of the school’s named game-day traditions.
cards.evidence_claim: Northwestern’s history page identifies making the “wildcat growl and claw” as a Northwestern football game-day tradition, and Athletics publishes the Wildcat Growl with its official songs.
cards.access_notes: Use it in the context of official sporting events and follow venue instructions.

cards.title: Join Primal Scream
cards.subtitle: Sunday before finals week, 9 p.m.
cards.notes: If you want to participate, keep it brief and considerate of residence-hall quiet hours, neighbors and any current campus guidance.
cards.short_summary: A synchronized end-of-quarter yell marks the approach of finals.
cards.evidence_claim: Northwestern’s WildWords dictionary defines Primal Scream as students screaming at exactly 9 p.m. on the Sunday before finals week each quarter to relieve stress and calls it uniquely Northwestern.
cards.access_notes: The documented timing is 9 p.m. on the Sunday before finals week; be mindful of local noise rules and others nearby.

cards.title: Volunteer at Project Pumpkin
cards.subtitle: Norris University Center, Halloween season
cards.notes: Watch for the organizer’s current volunteer call, then help host a supervised activity or welcome local children at an assigned booth.
cards.short_summary: Students create a Halloween celebration for children from Evanston and Chicago.
cards.evidence_claim: Northwestern reports that Project Pumpkin is an annual student-run Halloween celebration at Norris University Center, sponsored by Northwestern Community Development Corps since the late 1980s.
cards.source_title: Closeup: Project Pumpkin Organizers Report Record Turnout
cards.access_notes: Volunteer roles and event logistics are set annually; verify the current organizer’s instructions before participating.
